evidence: Analysis by X-ray diffraction (XRD) shows that the films are deposited with an essentially amorphous microstructure, but subsequent annealing above 700 °C in dry air crystallizes the films into the a- or monoclinic phase. Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) shows that residual carbon (0–5 at.- %) is present in the oxide films and that the HfO2 films grown by MOCVD generally contain more carbon than those grown by ALD. The dielectric properties of the as-deposited HfO2 films are evaluated using [Al/HfO2/SiO2/n-Si] MOS capacitor structures with various HfO2 thicknesses ranging from 1.7 nm to 102 nm. The carbon levels in the MOCVD-grown HfO2 films are comparable to the carbon impurities detected when using precursors such as [Hf(OtBu)2(dmop)2] (4.95 at.- %), [Hf(dmop)4] (4.15 at.- %), and [Hf(OtBu)2(mmp)2] (4.4 at.- %). The atomic composition of the hafnium oxide films was determined by AES, and the data are shown in Table 1. Medium energy ion scattering (MEIS) experiments were carried out at the CCLRC Daresbury MEIS facility on samples 864 and 834.
